summary: Task-workflow throughput, latency and journal integrity under concurrency, measured against a service built from this mold snapshot on a private, throwaway Postgres.
not_covered: Thread-open latency for a signed-in operator. NOT COVERED, permanently, and not merely skipped. `scripts/operator/thread-open-perf.mjs` needs a Google ID token copied out of a signed-in browser's localStorage (or an emailed sign-in code): lib/ops-auth.ts admits exactly those two human identities and says so — "There is deliberately no shared service key: every caller is a real, named human" — and such a token lives about an hour. No factory script can mint one for a stamped app, and asking a non-technical operator to open a browser console is not an instruction this factory gives. The check used to sit in `checks` guarded by an ops-token variable whose name appears NOWHERE in the mold (the script reads --token, --token-file or WORKSPACE_GOOGLE_TOKEN), so setting it would have run an unauthenticated baseline that exits 0 having measured no thread open at all — a `pass` with nothing behind it — and, with WORKSPACE_OPS_URL unset, against the LIVE projects rather than this app. See README.md for what would have to change for it to become measurable.

The DEPLOYED application. This lane builds services/task-workflow from the mold snapshot and runs it on this machine against a local Postgres; it does not touch the app's Vercel deployment or its database, so it measures the mold's engine, not the hosting.
GLM 5.2 inference throughput and the sandbox prewarm saturation budget — neither has a harness yet (mold_v1 backlog).
Concurrent multi-workspace chat load: the scenario drives one org's task workflow, not many workspaces at once (mold_v1 backlog).
Sustained soak. The spec is a burst of about four seconds, not an hour, so connection-pool exhaustion, leaks and autovacuum pressure are outside what any row here can claim.

checks.name: test:task-workflow:stress
checks.why: The task-workflow service is the multiplayer engine; p95 latency, throughput, HTTP errors and an intact transition journal under concurrency are what an operator feels.
